title: Project Critical Path Length
description:
Tasks have durations and predecessor edges. Walk every path from tasks with no dependency to the sinks and return the **longest path length** (critical path in days).

**Tables:** `tasks` (`task_id`, `duration`), `deps` (`task_id`, `depends_on`)

Output one row: `critical_path_days`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE tasks (task_id VARCHAR, duration INT); INSERT INTO tasks VALUES ('A',3),('B',2),('C',4),('D',2),('E',1),('F',3); CREATE TABLE deps (task_id VARCHAR, depends_on VARCHAR); INSERT INTO deps VALUES ('B','A'),('C','A'),('D','B'),('E','C'),('F','D'),('F','E');
solution_sql: WITH RECURSIVE paths AS (SELECT t.task_id, t.duration AS total FROM tasks t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deps d WHERE d.task_id = t.task_id) UNION ALL SELECT t.task_id, p.total + t.duration FROM paths p JOIN deps d ON d.depends_on = p.task_id JOIN tasks t ON t.task_id = d.task_id) SELECT MAX(total) AS critical_path_days FROM paths
hints: Anchor on tasks that do not appear as task_id in deps (no predecessors).
Recursive join deps.depends_on = current task, add duration, then MAX the totals.
explanation: Two complete paths reach F: A-B-D-F (3+2+2+3=10) and A-C-E-F (3+4+1+3=11). The critical path is 11 days. F has two predecessors so both paths are explored.
